findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a Forge source checkout is behind a release that adds a setting and changes a shipped template. The repaired comparison allows the merge, but `sync.refresh_merged_guides` then calls the old process's `repo.config(top)` at src/forge/sync.py:603-609. That parser rejects the unfamiliar setting before the handoff at src/forge/close.py:245, so close still stops instead of continuing under the newly pinned release.
findings.title: Avoid validating default-branch settings before the merge

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a working branch and an incoming upgrade both refresh a generated guide, causing a conflict. The revised test installs a pre-commit hook, but its working branch changes only `app.py` (tests/test_close.py:228-232), so its incoming merge is clean. [Git](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks) runs pre-merge-commit for that merge; Forge installs pre-commit and pre-push, not pre-merge-commit (src/forge/githooks.py:65). A generated-file conflict instead reaches `git commit` at src/forge/close.py:810, where a broken incoming-pin handoff in the real pre-commit hook would reject the new settings while both revised cases still pass. The existing changed-pin conflict proof explicitly has no installed pre-commit hook (tests/test_running_commands_follow_changed_forge_pin.py:194-199).
